title: Accountants and auditors
rationale: Purely digital/office knowledge work with no physical component for robots to automate. Work involves examining financial records, computing taxes, and advising clients—all cognitive tasks.

title: Actors
rationale: Acting is fundamentally about human embodied performance, emotional expression, and creative interpretation. While CGI and digital doubles exist, the core value is human physical and emotional presence. Robots cannot replace the artistic craft.

title: Actuaries
rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work involving mathematics, statistics, and financial modeling. No physical component whatsoever for robotic automation.

title: Administrative services and facilities managers
rationale: Primarily office-based management and coordination work. Minor physical component in facilities inspection, but core role is planning, directing, and decision-making—cognitive tasks with negligible physical automation potential.

title: Adult basic and secondary education and ESL teachers
rationale: Teaching involves in-person human interaction, emotional connection, and adaptive pedagogy. While some instruction can be digitized, the physical classroom presence and personal mentoring relationship is the core value. Minimal physical task content for robots.

title: Advertising sales agents
rationale: Entirely relationship-based sales work involving client meetings, presentations, and negotiations. No meaningful physical tasks for robotic automation.

title: Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers
rationale: Strategic management and creative direction work that is entirely cognitive. No physical labor component for robots to address.

title: Aerospace engineering and operations technologists and technicians
rationale: Significant hands-on work installing, testing, and maintaining aerospace equipment. By 2036, robots handle much of the routine installation and calibration, but the high-precision, safety-critical, and variable nature of aerospace work still requires human oversight and judgment for novel test configurations.

title: Aerospace engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and computational work. Physical prototyping and testing increasingly automated but the core engineering role is cognitive. Minor physical component in inspections.

title: Agricultural and food science technicians
rationale: Lab and field work involving sample collection, testing, and equipment operation. By 2036, much routine laboratory analysis and field sampling is automated. Humans remain for novel experimental setups and interpreting unexpected results.

title: Agricultural and food scientists
rationale: Primarily research and analytical work with some fieldwork and laboratory components. The physical aspects (field sampling, lab experiments) are partially automatable, but the core scientific judgment and research design are cognitive.

title: Agricultural engineers
rationale: Primarily design and engineering work that is cognitive. Some site visits and field testing, but the core role is problem-solving and system design rather than physical labor.

title: Agricultural workers
rationale: By 2036, commercial agriculture is heavily automated with robotic harvesting, planting, and tending for most crops. Remaining human roles are for genuinely novel situations, delicate specialty crops, and supervisory functions. The vast majority of routine field labor is robot-performed.

title: Air traffic controllers
rationale: Primarily a cognitive/digital monitoring and decision-making role. While physically located in towers, the work is screen-based coordination. Already heavily computerized; physical embodiment irrelevant.

title: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians
rationale: Hands-on maintenance and repair in complex, variable environments. By 2036, robots assist with routine inspections and standardized repairs, but aircraft maintenance involves highly variable configurations, tight spaces, and safety-critical judgment that still requires significant human involvement.

title: Airline and commercial pilots
rationale: Autonomous flight systems handle most routine operations by 2036. Regulatory and safety requirements still mandate human pilots, but their role is increasingly supervisory. Humans essential for genuinely novel emergencies and edge cases.

title: Animal care and service workers
rationale: Working with live animals in variable environments requires adaptability to unpredictable animal behavior. By 2036, robots handle routine feeding and cleaning in structured facilities, but grooming, training, and handling diverse animals still needs significant human involvement due to animal variability and emotional bonding.

title: Announcers and DJs
rationale: Entirely voice/personality/communication work. No physical labor component. AI voice synthesis is a digital AI issue, not physical/embodied.

title: Anthropologists and archeologists
rationale: Fieldwork involves working in highly unstructured, novel environments (excavation sites, remote communities). The physical components of archeological digs occur in genuinely unpredictable terrain. Primarily cognitive research and analysis work.

title: Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators
rationale: Entirely interpersonal and cognitive work involving negotiation, judgment, and conflict resolution. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Architects
rationale: Primarily creative design and planning work that is cognitive. Site visits involve observation rather than physical labor. CAD and modeling tools are digital, not robotic.

title: Architectural and engineering managers
rationale: Management and coordination role that is entirely cognitive. Planning, directing teams, and making strategic decisions. No physical labor component.

title: Archivists, curators, and museum workers
rationale: Conservation work involves delicate handling of unique, irreplaceable artifacts requiring fine motor skills and aesthetic judgment. Museum installation has some automatable components, but the variability and preciousness of objects limits robotic handling. Curatorial work is primarily cognitive.

title: Art directors
rationale: Creative direction and visual design management is entirely cognitive work. Decision-making about visual aesthetics, managing creative teams. No physical labor.

title: Assemblers and fabricators
rationale: Repetitive assembly work in structured manufacturing environments is highly automatable by 2036. Robots handle the vast majority of assembly tasks. Remaining human roles are supervisory and for genuinely novel or very low-volume custom work.

title: Athletes and sports competitors
rationale: Athletic competition is inherently about human physical performance. The entire value proposition is humans competing physically. Robots cannot substitute for human athletes in sports.

title: Athletic trainers
rationale: Hands-on physical assessment, rehabilitation exercises, and injury treatment involving direct human contact. The therapeutic relationship and adaptive physical manipulation based on patient response requires human presence, though diagnostic equipment is increasingly automated.

title: Atmospheric scientists, including meteorologists
rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work involving data analysis, modeling, and forecasting. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Audiologists
rationale: Clinical work involving patient interaction, physical examination of ears, fitting hearing devices. Requires human trust and communication. Some diagnostic testing is automatable, but the patient relationship and adaptive clinical judgment remain human-centered.

title: Automotive body and glass repairers
rationale: By 2036, many standardized body repairs and glass replacements are robot-performed in structured shop environments. However, damage assessment and repair of complex, unique damage patterns still requires human judgment. Robots handle most routine panel and glass work.

title: Automotive service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Vehicle repair involves significant diagnostic work and physical manipulation in variable configurations. By 2036, robots handle many standardized maintenance tasks (oil changes, tire rotations, brake replacements), but diagnosing complex problems and working on varied vehicle models still requires significant human involvement.

title: Bakers
rationale: Commercial baking in production environments is highly automated by 2036. Robots handle mixing, shaping, baking, and packaging for standard products. Artisanal and custom baking retains some human craft, but the vast majority of commercial baking is robot-operated.

title: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists
rationale: Haircutting and styling involves intimate personal contact where the human relationship IS the product for many clients. High variability in hair types, styles, and client preferences. By 2036, basic cuts might be robot-assisted, but the personal service, aesthetic judgment, and client relationship keep this predominantly human.

title: Bartenders
rationale: By 2036, robotic bartending systems handle standard drink preparation efficiently. However, the social/entertainment aspect of bartending, customer interaction, and craft cocktail culture retain human value. High-volume venues largely automated; craft and hospitality-focused venues retain humans.

title: Bill and account collectors
rationale: Entirely communication-based work involving phone calls, negotiations, and record-keeping. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Biochemists and biophysicists
rationale: Laboratory research involves physical manipulation of equipment and samples, but the core work is cognitive research and analysis. By 2036, lab automation handles much routine experimentation, but novel research setups and experimental design remain human-driven.

title: Bioengineers and biomedical engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and research work that is cognitive. Some prototype testing and lab work, but the core engineering role involves minimal physical labor that robots would address.

title: Biological technicians
rationale: Lab work involving sample preparation, equipment operation, and routine testing. By 2036, much laboratory processing is automated. Humans remain for novel experimental procedures and equipment troubleshooting in variable research contexts.

title: Boilermakers
rationale: Heavy industrial work in variable environments (power plants, refineries). By 2036, robots handle much welding and assembly in accessible locations, but boilermaker work often involves confined spaces, variable site conditions, and safety-critical judgment. Significant but not complete automation.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks
rationale: Entirely digital/office work involving financial record-keeping. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Broadcast, sound, and video technicians
rationale: Equipment setup, operation, and maintenance involves physical work in variable environments (studios, live events). By 2036, some routine setup is automated, but live production environments are highly variable and require adaptive problem-solving with physical equipment.

title: Budget analysts
rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work. No physical component whatsoever.

title: Bus drivers
rationale: By 2036, autonomous vehicles handle most fixed-route bus operations. Remaining human drivers are for genuinely challenging routes, extreme weather, and passenger safety/assistance needs. Urban and suburban fixed routes are largely autonomous.

title: Butchers
rationale: By 2036, most commercial meat cutting and processing is robotic, with advanced vision systems and dexterous manipulation handling varied animal anatomy. Custom butchering for specialty markets retains some human craft, but volume operations are heavily automated.

title: Calibration technologists and technicians
rationale: Routine calibration of instruments and equipment is highly automatable in structured environments. By 2036, robots handle most standard calibration procedures. Humans remain for novel equipment, troubleshooting, and field calibration in variable environments.

title: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians
rationale: Patient-facing diagnostic work involving equipment operation and patient positioning. By 2036, much imaging is automated, but patient interaction, positioning of varied body types, and adaptive testing still require human involvement. Regulatory requirements also mandate human presence.

title: Career and technical education teachers
rationale: Teaching involves hands-on demonstration and student mentoring in workshop environments. The educational relationship and adaptive instruction are human-centered. Physical demonstration of trades skills and supervising student practice requires human presence and judgment.

title: Carpenters
rationale: Residential and commercial carpentry involves highly variable work environments, custom measurements, and adaptation to existing structures. By 2036, robots handle many standardized framing and installation tasks, but custom work, renovation, and site-specific adaptation still require significant human skill and judgment.

title: Cartographers and photogrammetrists
rationale: Primarily digital/analytical work involving GIS software, remote sensing data, and map creation. Minimal physical component—some field surveying but mostly screen-based work.

title: Cashiers
rationale: Self-checkout and automated retail systems are ubiquitous by 2036. Most transaction processing is fully automated. Remaining human cashiers serve primarily social/customer-service functions in select retail environments.

title: Chefs and head cooks
rationale: Head chefs are primarily creative and managerial. Menu design, recipe development, quality oversight, and kitchen management are cognitive tasks. By 2036, robots handle much routine food preparation, but creative culinary work, taste judgment, and kitchen leadership remain human-centered.

title: Chemical engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and process optimization work that is cognitive. Site visits and plant inspections have minor physical components, but the core role is engineering problem-solving.

title: Chemical technicians
rationale: Laboratory and plant work involving routine testing, sample preparation, and equipment operation. By 2036, much routine chemical analysis and process monitoring is automated. Humans remain for novel procedures and troubleshooting.

title: Chemists and materials scientists
rationale: Research work with significant lab components. By 2036, routine lab procedures are automated, but novel experimental design and research requiring creative physical manipulation of materials remains human-driven. Core work is cognitive analysis.

title: Childcare workers
rationale: Childcare is fundamentally about human emotional presence, safety, and nurturing relationships. Children require human warmth, adaptability, and emotional intelligence. By 2036, robots may assist with monitoring and routine tasks, but the core caregiving role demands human presence and intimacy.

title: Chiropractors
rationale: Hands-on physical manipulation therapy where human touch and adaptive physical response to patient feedback IS the treatment. By 2036, some diagnostic imaging is automated, but the core spinal manipulation and patient relationship remains human-centered.

title: Civil engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Field testing, site inspection, and laboratory work with physical components. By 2036, some routine testing and surveying is automated, but variable field conditions and site-specific judgment require human involvement. Mix of office analysis and fieldwork.

title: Civil engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and project management work. Site visits involve observation and assessment rather than physical labor. Core work is cognitive engineering problem-solving.

title: Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators
rationale: Primarily analytical work with some field inspection. By 2036, drone and robotic inspection assists with physical site assessment, but the investigative judgment and human interaction for claims assessment remain cognitive. Limited physical component.

title: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians
rationale: By 2036, clinical laboratory analysis is highly automated with robotic sample handling, analysis, and reporting. Most routine blood work, urinalysis, and microbiological testing is fully automated. Humans remain for complex or unusual samples and quality oversight.

title: Coaches and scouts
rationale: Coaching is about human motivation, strategic thinking, and interpersonal leadership. Physical demonstration is a minor component. The core value is human relationship, inspiration, and tactical judgment. Scouting involves observation and evaluation.

title: Community health workers
rationale: Work centers on community relationships, health education, and connecting people with services. Requires cultural competency, empathy, and trust-building. Minimal physical tasks; mostly interpersonal and cognitive.

title: Compensation and benefits managers
rationale: Entirely office-based management and analytical work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists
rationale: Entirely analytical and administrative work. No physical component.

title: Compliance officers
rationale: Primarily analytical and investigative work reviewing records and procedures. Some facility inspections have minor physical components, but the core role is regulatory knowledge and judgment.

title: Computer and information research scientists
rationale: Purely cognitive research and computational work. No physical component whatsoever.

title: Computer and information systems managers
rationale: Management and strategic planning role that is entirely cognitive. No physical labor component.

title: Computer hardware engineers
rationale: Primarily design work that is cognitive, with some physical prototyping and testing. By 2036, much hardware testing is automated, but novel prototype evaluation still has a human physical component. Core role is design and analysis.

title: Computer network architects
rationale: Entirely design and planning work for network systems. No physical labor component.

title: Computer programmers
rationale: Purely digital/cognitive work. No physical component whatsoever.

title: Computer support specialists
rationale: Mix of remote and on-site support. On-site hardware troubleshooting has physical components. By 2036, remote diagnostics handle most issues, and physical hardware work is increasingly standardized. Some hands-on work in variable office environments remains.

title: Computer systems analysts
rationale: Entirely analytical and consulting work. No physical component.

title: Concierges
rationale: Primarily interpersonal service providing recommendations and assistance. The human touch and personal relationship is central to the role. Minimal physical tasks; mostly communication and knowledge-based.

title: Conservation scientists and foresters
rationale: Fieldwork in natural environments involves physical data collection and site assessment. By 2036, drones and sensors automate much monitoring, but working in unstructured natural environments for conservation assessment still requires human judgment and physical presence in novel terrain.

title: Construction and building inspectors
rationale: Site inspections involve navigating variable construction environments and making safety/compliance judgments. By 2036, drones and robotic sensors assist with data collection, but the interpretive judgment in highly variable building conditions still requires human expertise. Physical access to varied sites remains challenging for robots.

title: Construction equipment operators
rationale: By 2036, autonomous construction equipment handles most grading, excavation, and material moving on well-mapped sites. Human operators remain for genuinely novel terrain, urban environments with complex obstacles, and oversight of autonomous operations.

title: Construction laborers and helpers
rationale: General construction labor involves varied physical tasks in changing environments. By 2036, robots handle much material moving, concrete work, and repetitive tasks. But the high variability of construction sites and need for adaptive physical work means significant human involvement remains for site-specific challenges.

title: Construction managers
rationale: Primarily management, planning, and coordination work. Site visits involve observation rather than physical labor. Core role is project management, budgeting, and team leadership—cognitive tasks.

title: Cooks
rationale: By 2036, robotic cooking systems handle most restaurant and institutional food preparation for standard menu items. Human cooks remain for creative dishes, quality oversight, and adaptation to ingredient variability. High-volume, standardized cooking environments are largely automated.

title: Correctional officers and bailiffs
rationale: Security work requiring human judgment, authority, and physical presence for inmate management. By 2036, surveillance is heavily automated, but the human authority, de-escalation skills, and physical intervention capability remain necessary. Regulatory and ethical requirements mandate human presence.

title: Cost estimators
rationale: Entirely analytical work involving calculations, project assessment, and financial modeling. No physical component.

title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
rationale: Entirely transcription and recording work. No physical component relevant to robotics.

title: Craft and fine artists
rationale: Artistic creation is fundamentally about human creative expression and aesthetic judgment with unique materials. The physical craft IS the art. By 2036, robotic tools may assist, but the creative vision and manual artistry remain inherently human.

title: Credit counselors
rationale: Entirely interpersonal counseling and financial advisory work. No physical component.

title: Customer service representatives
rationale: Primarily communication-based work via phone, chat, or in-person. Physical component is negligible. Digital AI handles most automation, not physical robots.

title: Dancers and choreographers
rationale: Dance is fundamentally human physical artistic expression. The entire value is human bodily movement and creative expression. Robots cannot substitute for human dancers in artistic performance.

title: Data scientists
rationale: Purely computational and analytical work. No physical component whatsoever.

title: Database administrators and architects
rationale: Entirely digital/technical work managing database systems. No physical component.

title: Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers
rationale: By 2036, autonomous delivery vehicles handle most mapped-route deliveries. Last-mile delivery robots are widespread. Human drivers remain for unmapped areas, customer interaction for sales, and genuinely novel delivery scenarios. The vast majority of routine delivery is automated.

title: Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians
rationale: By 2036, manufacturing of dental prosthetics, lenses, and medical appliances is highly automated with precision robotics and 3D printing. Custom fitting and adjustment work retains some human involvement, but production is largely robotic.

title: Dental assistants
rationale: Patient-facing clinical support involving handing instruments, suctioning, and patient comfort during procedures. By 2036, robotic assistance handles some routine tasks, but the patient interaction, adaptive support during variable procedures, and human comfort provision require continued human presence.

title: Dental hygienists
rationale: Hands-on cleaning and examination inside patients' mouths requires dexterity and patient interaction. By 2036, robotic cleaning tools may assist, but the intimate oral care, patient communication, and adaptive clinical judgment in variable oral conditions keep significant human involvement.

title: Dentists
rationale: Complex oral procedures requiring fine dexterity, patient relationship, and clinical judgment. By 2036, robotic systems assist with standardized procedures, but complex restorative work, diagnosis of novel conditions, and patient management remain human-centered. Regulatory requirements also mandate human oversight.

title: Desktop publishers
rationale: Entirely digital design and layout work. No physical component.

title: Diagnostic medical sonographers
rationale: Operating ultrasound equipment requires physical manipulation of the probe on patients with varied body types. By 2036, automated scanning assists, but adaptive probe positioning and real-time diagnostic interpretation during scanning still requires human skill and patient interaction.

title: Diesel service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Heavy vehicle repair involves physical work in variable conditions. By 2036, robots handle many standardized maintenance procedures, but diagnosing complex problems on diverse diesel equipment and working in field conditions still requires significant human involvement.

title: Dietitians and nutritionists
rationale: Primarily counseling and analytical work involving meal planning and health education. No meaningful physical component for robotic automation.

title: Drafters
rationale: Entirely CAD and digital design work. No physical component.

title: Drywall installers, ceiling tile installers, and tapers
rationale: By 2036, robotic systems handle much standardized drywall installation in new construction with uniform layouts. However, renovation work, complex ceiling configurations, and finishing/taping in variable conditions still require human skill. Significant automation of routine installation.

title: Economists
rationale: Entirely analytical and research work. No physical component whatsoever.

title: Editors
rationale: Entirely cognitive work involving reading, writing, and editorial judgment. No physical component.

title: Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on testing, building prototypes, and troubleshooting electronic equipment. By 2036, routine testing is automated, but working with novel prototypes and diagnosing complex faults in variable equipment still requires human dexterity and judgment.

title: Electrical and electronics engineers
rationale: Primarily design and analysis work that is cognitive. Minor hands-on prototyping component. Core role is engineering problem-solving.

title: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
rationale: Installation and repair work in variable environments. By 2036, robots handle standardized installations, but troubleshooting complex electrical systems in diverse settings (industrial, commercial) still requires human diagnostic skill and adaptive physical work.

title: Electrical power-line installers and repairers
rationale: Working on power lines involves climbing poles, working at heights, and navigating outdoor environments in all conditions. By 2036, drones and climbing robots assist significantly, but the variability of outdoor conditions, emergency repair scenarios, and working on energized systems still requires substantial human involvement.

title: Electricians
rationale: Residential and commercial electrical work involves highly variable environments—every building is different. By 2036, robots handle standardized new-construction wiring, but renovation work, troubleshooting in existing buildings, and adapting to unique configurations require significant human judgment and dexterity.

title: Electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
rationale: Testing and maintaining electro-mechanical equipment. By 2036, routine maintenance and testing procedures are automated, but troubleshooting complex integrated systems in variable industrial environments retains human involvement for novel fault diagnosis.

title: Elementary, middle, and high school principals
rationale: Management and leadership role involving strategic planning, staff management, and community relations. Entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical labor component.

title: Elevator and escalator installers and repairers
rationale: Specialized work in confined, vertical spaces with safety-critical requirements. By 2036, standardized installations benefit from robotic assistance, but the variability of building shafts, retrofitting older buildings, and safety-critical troubleshooting still require significant human skill.

title: Emergency management directors
rationale: Entirely planning, coordination, and management work. No physical labor component.

title: EMTs and paramedics
rationale: Emergency medical response in highly unstructured, unpredictable environments. Every scene is different—accident sites, homes, public spaces. By 2036, robotic medical equipment assists, but the chaotic, variable nature of emergency scenes and need for rapid human judgment and intimate patient contact keep this predominantly human.

title: Entertainment and recreation managers
rationale: Management and planning role that is entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical labor component.

title: Environmental engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Field sampling, monitoring, and testing in varied environmental sites. By 2036, automated monitoring handles much routine data collection, but site-specific environmental assessment in novel locations still requires human judgment and physical presence.

title: Environmental engineers
rationale: Primarily design and analytical engineering work. Some site visits but core role is cognitive problem-solving and regulatory compliance analysis.

title: Environmental science and protection technicians
rationale: Field work collecting samples and monitoring conditions in varied natural and industrial environments. By 2036, automated monitoring handles routine sampling, but novel site assessment and working in unstructured environments still requires human presence.

title: Environmental scientists and specialists
rationale: Primarily analytical and research work with some fieldwork. The physical field components (sampling, site assessment) are partially automatable with drones and sensors, but the core scientific analysis and regulatory judgment are cognitive.

title: Epidemiologists
rationale: Entirely analytical and research work involving data analysis and disease investigation. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Exercise physiologists
rationale: Hands-on patient assessment and exercise program implementation. Requires physical demonstration, patient motivation, and adaptive response to individual patient conditions. By 2036, monitoring equipment is automated, but the personal guidance and physical interaction remain human-centered.

title: Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers
rationale: Management role with significant physical oversight component. By 2036, most farming operations are automated, but managers must still make judgment calls about variable conditions, animal welfare, and novel situations. Physical presence for inspection and decision-making in variable environments.

title: Fashion designers
rationale: Primarily creative design work that is cognitive. Prototype creation and fitting have physical components, but the core value is aesthetic vision and trend interpretation.

title: Film and video editors and camera operators
rationale: Editing is entirely digital. Camera operation involves physical manipulation of equipment in variable environments. By 2036, some automated camera systems exist, but creative cinematography requires human artistic judgment about movement, framing, and timing.

title: Financial analysts
rationale: Entirely analytical and computational work. No physical component.

title: Financial clerks
rationale: Office-based administrative work. No meaningful physical component for robotic automation.

title: Financial examiners
rationale: Entirely analytical and investigative work reviewing financial records. No physical component.

title: Financial managers
rationale: Management and strategic financial planning. Entirely cognitive work.

title: Fire inspectors
rationale: Site inspections in variable environments (burned buildings, construction sites). By 2036, drones and sensors assist with data collection, but investigating fire scenes in structurally compromised buildings requires human judgment in truly unstructured environments.

title: Firefighters
rationale: Emergency response in highly unstructured, dangerous, and unpredictable environments. Every fire scene is novel. By 2036, robotic firefighting assists in some structured scenarios, but search and rescue in burning buildings, wildland fire, and complex emergency scenes remain predominantly human due to extreme environmental unpredictability.

title: Fishing and hunting workers
rationale: Fishing involves highly variable natural environments—weather, sea conditions, fish behavior. By 2036, commercial fishing vessels benefit from significant automation for net handling and processing, but the unpredictable ocean environment and real-time adaptation to conditions require human judgment.

title: Fitness trainers and instructors
rationale: Personal training involves human motivation, relationship, physical demonstration, and adaptive coaching. The personal connection and motivational presence IS the product for many clients. By 2036, robotic exercise equipment exists, but the human trainer's role as motivator and form corrector remains valued.

title: Flight attendants
rationale: In-cabin service involves passenger interaction, safety management, and working in confined variable environments. By 2036, routine beverage/food service may be partially automated, but passenger safety, emergency response, and customer service in the variable cabin environment require human presence. Regulatory requirements also mandate humans.

title: Flooring installers and tile and stone setters
rationale: Flooring and tile work involves variable substrates, custom patterns, and adaptation to room geometry. By 2036, robots handle standardized large-area flooring installation, but custom tile work, complex patterns, and renovation in irregular spaces still require significant human skill.

title: Floral designers
rationale: Creative arrangement of natural materials with high variability. Each flower is unique. By 2036, basic bouquet assembly may be automated, but creative custom design requiring aesthetic judgment with variable natural materials remains human-centered.

title: Food and beverage serving and related workers
rationale: By 2036, robotic serving systems are common in many restaurant and institutional settings. Automated ordering, food delivery robots, and self-service are widespread. Human servers persist in fine dining and hospitality-focused venues where personal service is the product.

title: Food preparation workers
rationale: Routine food preparation—chopping, portioning, basic cooking—is highly automated by 2036. Robotic food prep systems handle standardized tasks in institutional and fast-food settings. Humans remain for creative preparation and quality oversight.

title: Food processing equipment workers
rationale: Food processing in factory environments is highly automated by 2036 with robotic handling, sorting, and processing equipment. Standardized production lines run with minimal human intervention. Humans remain primarily for oversight and maintenance.

title: Food service managers
rationale: Management role involving planning, staff supervision, and quality control. Physical inspection of food and facilities is a component, but the core role is cognitive management and decision-making. By 2036, automated monitoring assists, but managerial judgment remains human.

title: Forensic science technicians
rationale: Crime scene investigation involves working in highly variable, unstructured environments. By 2036, lab analysis is heavily automated, but crime scene evidence collection in novel, unpredictable settings still requires human judgment and careful physical work.

title: Forest and conservation workers
rationale: Outdoor work in unstructured natural environments—every forest site is different. By 2036, automated equipment handles some routine operations, but the variable terrain, weather conditions, and ecological judgment required in conservation work keep significant human involvement.

title: Fundraisers
rationale: Entirely interpersonal and strategic work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Funeral service workers
rationale: Funeral services involve intimate human care, emotional sensitivity, and handling of deceased with dignity. By 2036, some preparation procedures may be partially automated, but the deeply personal and emotional nature of the work, along with the physical care requiring human sensitivity, keeps this predominantly human.

title: Gambling services workers
rationale: Casino and gaming operations involve equipment operation and customer interaction in structured environments. By 2036, many gaming floor operations are automated (slot machines, automated table games), but the customer service and entertainment aspects retain human presence.

title: General maintenance and repair workers
rationale: Wide variety of repair tasks in variable building environments. By 2036, robots handle many routine maintenance tasks (changing filters, basic plumbing, painting), but the extreme variability of maintenance requests across diverse buildings and systems requires human adaptability for novel problems.

title: General office clerks
rationale: Entirely office-based administrative work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Genetic counselors
rationale: Entirely cognitive and interpersonal counseling work. No physical component.

title: Geographers
rationale: Primarily research and analytical work. Minimal physical fieldwork; mostly computational and GIS-based.

title: Geological and hydrologic technicians
rationale: Field sampling and testing in variable geological environments. By 2036, automated sampling equipment handles routine collection, but working in novel geological settings and interpreting site conditions still requires human judgment and physical presence.

title: Geoscientists
rationale: Primarily research and analytical work with some fieldwork. Physical field components are partially automatable, but the core scientific analysis is cognitive.

title: Glaziers
rationale: Glass installation involves working with heavy, fragile materials in variable building environments. By 2036, robots assist with large commercial installations, but residential work, renovation, and custom configurations still require human dexterity and judgment.

title: Graphic designers
rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Grounds maintenance workers
rationale: By 2036, robotic mowing, trimming, and basic landscaping of uniform areas is widespread. Autonomous grounds maintenance equipment handles most routine tasks. Human workers remain for complex landscape design implementation and genuinely novel environments.

title: Hand laborers and material movers
rationale: By 2036, material handling in warehouses, factories, and loading docks is overwhelmingly automated. Robotic lifting, sorting, and moving equipment handles the vast majority of tasks. Human involvement is marginal—supervisory and for genuinely unusual items or situations.

title: Hazardous materials removal workers
rationale: Hazmat work involves variable and dangerous environments. By 2036, robotic systems handle many routine hazmat removal tasks (asbestos, lead paint in accessible areas), but complex contamination scenarios in unstructured environments still require human judgment. The danger actually accelerates robot adoption.

title: Health and safety engineers
rationale: Primarily analytical and design work focused on workplace safety systems. Site inspections have minor physical components, but core role is cognitive engineering and regulatory compliance.

title: Health education specialists
rationale: Entirely educational and interpersonal work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Health information technologists and medical registrars
rationale: Entirely digital/data management work. No physical component.

title: Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
rationale: HVAC work involves variable building environments and diverse equipment configurations. By 2036, robots handle standardized new-construction installations, but diagnosing problems in existing systems and working in varied building spaces (attics, crawlspaces, rooftops) requires human judgment and adaptability.

title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers
rationale: By 2036, autonomous long-haul trucking on mapped highways is the norm. Human drivers remain primarily for unmapped last-mile delivery, extreme weather, and genuinely novel route conditions. The vast majority of interstate freight moves autonomously.

title: Heavy vehicle and mobile equipment service technicians
rationale: Maintaining heavy equipment involves physical work on large, variable machines in diverse environments. By 2036, diagnostic automation and robotic maintenance assist with routine service, but field repairs on diverse equipment in variable conditions require significant human involvement.

title: High school teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally about human relationships, mentoring, and adaptive instruction. Physical classroom presence, managing student behavior, and providing emotional support are central. Minimal physical task content for robots; the human connection is the value.

title: Historians
rationale: Entirely research and analytical work. No physical component.

title: Home health and personal care aides

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Entirely sales and relationship work. No physical component for robotic automation.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Working at extreme heights on variable equipment in outdoor conditions. By 2036, drone inspection and some robotic maintenance assist, but the variable conditions, heights, and complex turbine systems still require significant human skill and judgment.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: By 2036, CNC and robotic woodworking handle most production furniture and cabinet making. Custom, artistic, and restoration woodworking retains human craftsmanship, but volume production is heavily automated.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Entirely cognitive and creative work. No physical component.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: Fieldwork in natural environments with unpredictable wildlife. By 2036, remote monitoring (drones, cameras) automates much data collection, but field research in unstructured environments with wild animals requires human judgment and physical presence.
